links.reason: Kainnilai 22 says only உள்ளம் பிரிந்தமை நீ அறிதி; whether it is a question or a statement is open, and nothing in it splits body from heart as Akananuru 29 does (உடம்பு ஆண்டு ஒழிந்தமை ... நெஞ்சம் நின் உழையதுவே). The 'shared assurance' exists only if the contested question reading is granted and the body half is supplied.

The kali refrain வானம் துளி மாறு பொழுதின் இவ் உலகம் போலும் நின் அளி மாறு பொழுதின் echoes the couplet's துளியின்மை ஞாலத்திற்கு ... அளியின்மை word for word, and applies the king's அளி to the husband. 'Failure of rule' stretches it a little, but the transfer from realm to wife is in the Tamil.

Kuruntokai 220 has the mullai buds opening at evening (குறுமுகை அவிழ்ந்த ... மாலையும் வாரார) and the couplet has a sickness that blossoms at evening (மாலை மலரும்), a real resonance. But the Kural names no flower, so the claim that its metaphor 'rests on' the jasmine land is unsupported, and the Kuruntokai poem does not say her grief opens.

Kalittokai 74 sets the bee moving from pond flower to neythal to lotus beside a man who joins one woman at forenoon and seeks others by afternoon, without a joining word; Thinaimozhi 35 says it openly, கூனிவண்டு அன்ன ... நல்லூரன், and adds the result, மேனி ஒழிய விடும். The hidden-versus-open contrast is true and specific.

Verse 2's வழுவும் வழு அல்ல and verse 17's குற்றம் குற்றமே நல்ல ஆகா do collide verbally. But 2 excuses faults in the poet's own words by the worth of the one praised, while 17 denies that a great bearer makes his own fault good; these are different faults, so the incompatibility is partial and the tension needs a generous reading.

The Paripadal story turns on two chests, நன்றா நட்ட அவன் நன் மார்பு முயங்கி and ஒன்றா நட்டவன் உறு வரை மார்பின், with no recitation; Thiruppugazh 870 has the child's நமநாராயணாய and the father's challenge before the pillar. The shift from embrace to uttered name is accurate, though in 870 it is a passing epithet.
links.text_issue: Paripadal 4 line 20 restored (ஒடு); lines 22-24 hard to construe.

links.reason: Kuruntokai 126 opens with the charge இளமை பாரார் வளநசைஇச் சென்றோர், and Ainkurunuru 415, in the decade of the returned man, answers with இனிதுடன் கழிக்கின் இளமை in the same mullai season. The two weigh youth from both sides of the parting, which neither shows alone.
links.text_issue: Ainkurunuru 415 line 4 அவர்ப் புணர்வு sits oddly in an address to மடந்தை.

links.reason: Both forbid the night visit with the same threat (இரவரின் வாழாளால் / வழிநாள் வாழ்குவள் அல்லள்), which is the shared stock situation of iravukkuri. The quatrain is not 'flat': its own prowling tiger (நீள்வேங்கை கொட்கும்) already gives the danger, so the claim that Akananuru 18 supplies a reason the short poem leaves out is overstated.

Kuruntokai 174's இவ் உலகத்துப் பொருளே மன்ற பொருளே அருளே மன்ற ஆருமில்லதுவே takes the same three terms as the couplet (இவ்வுலகம், பொருள், அருள்) and leaves grace ownerless, dropping the other-world half. The qualification is real; only the implied order of reply is doubtful.

Kural 228 says the hoarder (வைத்திழக்கும் வன்கணவர்) misses the joy of giving; the quatrain ranks him below the man with nothing (கைத்தில்லார் நல்லவர் கைத்துண்டாய்க் காப்பாரின்; வைத்தாரின் நல்லர் வறியவர்). The step from a missed joy to worse than poverty is in the Tamil.

The shared phrase is real (செய்த உதவி / செய்யாமல் செய்த உதவி), and the parrots' help is unmeant. But the Kural's point is help given without prior help, not deliberate help, and nothing in either verse says the debt becomes 'even less payable'; teaches invents its conclusion.

Kural 215's ஊருணி நீர்நிறைந்தற்றே is a simile for a wise man's wealth; Sirupanchamoolam 62's நீர்அறம் is the literal charity of giving water. The link turns only on the word water, and the verse does not take up the Kural's image at all.

Kural 1325 is concessive (தவறிலர் ஆயினும்), granting the man may be faultless; in Kalittokai 89 the man's தீதோ இலேன் is met with மருந்து இன்று and the expectation that he will fall at her feet saying தப்பினேன். That is a different situation, not an incompatible claim; the contrast qualifies the couplet rather than contradicting it.
links.text_issue: Speaker division in Kalittokai 89 lines 10-11 is uncertain.

links.reason: The open gate (அருங்கடி வாயில் அயிராது புகுமின்) against the shut door (பாடுநர்க்கு அடைத்த கதவின்) is a neat contrast, but it rests on making Malaipadukadam's Nannan son of Nannan the same house as Purananuru 151's பொலந்தேர் நன்னன், which neither poem states. Teaches itself admits the 'if'.

Kuruntokai 359's புதல்வற் றழீஇயினன் ... புதல்வன் தாய் அவன் புறங்கவைஇயினளே and Kalittokai 75's புதல்வன் புல்லிப் பொய் துயில் துஞ்சும் ... அவிந்து ஒழியும் என் புலவி show the same act, the father holding the son in bed. The pair shows it as both the sign and the instrument of reconciliation, which neither does alone.

Ainkurunuru 74's கரைசேர் மருதம் ஏறிப் பண்ணை பாய்வோள் and Purananuru 243's உயர்சினை மருதத் துறை ... படிகோடு ஏறி ... பாய்ந்து are the same distinctive leap. One freezes it as a woman's beauty, the other mourns it as lost youth (யாண்டுண்டு கொல்லோ), a real opposition of use.

Vengai, spear and midnight (இடையாமத்து / அரைநாள் இரவு) are stock iravukkuri furniture shared by two independent poems. Akananuru 298 is tangled and makes no clear plea for marriage, so the 'before and after' story and its moral are the grader's construction rather than the poems'.

கண்படை பெறாஅ and கண்படை இலனே is a genuine verbal echo, and Akananuru 214 does split the sleepless வேந்தன் from the speaker who says அமரும் நம்வயினதுவே. But the claim that Mullaippattu makes the husband the king rests on lines outside the printed span, which the marker flags as uncertain.

The grace-as-rain image is shared (துளி நசை வேட்கையான் மிசை பாடும் புள்ளின் தன் அளி நசை / வாழ்வார்க்கு வானம் ... அளி). But Kalittokai 46's stormy midnight (கனை பெயல் நடுநாள் யான் கண் மாற) is the man's complaint that she slept, not rain keeping him away, so the 'testing against the weather' irony is read in.

The tusker that eases its mate on the man's road is a stock paalai comfort; Kuruntokai 37 does name the road அன்பின, while Ainthinai Aimpathu 32 gives only the act. The stated-versus-implied difference is true but thin, and Aimpathu line 1 (செல்லாரோ வல்லர்) is too unclear to say what argument it makes.

Kural 70 speaks of what others say of a good son's father (என்நோற்றான் கொல்), not of a son resembling his father; Kalittokai 86's ஒத்தி ... ஒவ்வாதி is about likeness. The 'same likeness' that teaches turns on is not in the couplet, so the pair shares only the father-son topic.

செம்புற்று ஈயல் and நெடுஞ்செம் புற்றம் ஈயல் is a real shared image used differently. But the war-loving lord 'standing between' the two, home from a war where 'other men were the termites', is invented: Ainkurunuru 497 only says போர்வெம் குருசில் வந்த மாறே.

The same poet's formula (தந்தனை சென்மோ கொண்ட இவள் நலனே / நலம் தந்து சென்மே) is a real tie. But reading 159 as a push to marriage borrows Natrinai 395's colophon thurai (வரைவு கடாயது) for a claim 159 itself does not make; that is tradition about another poem.

Neighbouring verses by one poet share குறவர் மகளிரேம். In 8 what turns aside his pretext is the reply போந்தது இல் ஐய களிறு, not the self-naming, so 'naming the tribe is itself the refusal' holds for 6 (காணினும் காய்வர் எமர்) but not for 8.

Song 10 likens the river to the giving Vazhuthi (பொலம் சொரி வழுதியின்) and the fragment likens Maran bathing to Indra (இந்திரன் ஆடும் தகைத்து); both observations are accurate. The picture of the king 'standing between' river and heaven is the reader's arrangement of two songs by different hands, not something either says.

Song 8 has elephant, cock and cave answering (மாறுமாறு அதிர்ப்ப) with the lute only as a likeness for bees (யாழ் இசை கேழ்த்து அன்ன); song 17 sets the bards' lute, flute, drum and singers against bee, tumbi, falls and peacock in ten ஒருதிறம் sides, மாறு எதிர் கோடல். The move from a nature echo to musicians matched against the hill is in the Tamil.

links.reason: Kuruntokai 160's அன்றில் ... பேடையொடு ... நரலும் நள்ளென் யாமத்து and Akananuru 305's ஒரு தனி அன்றில் உயவுக்குரல் share the midnight anril in the north wind. One bird is paired and one alone, so the pair shows the same bird used as contrast and as likeness, which is specific and true.
links.text_issue: Akananuru 305 line 5 supplied from a commentary edition.

links.reason: மயில்கொல் மடவாள்கொல் ... தெய்வம்கொல் and அணங்குகொல் ஆய்மயில் கொல்லோ ... மாதர்கொல் are the same three-way doubt. The venba adds the place (இளஞாழல் பூம்பொழில்) and a goddess of the waves (மாநீர்த் திரையுள் பயில்வதோர் தெய்வம்), which teaches states accurately.

பட்டினம் பெறினும் ... வாரேன் and உலகம் அமிழ்தொடு பெறினும் ... நீடலோ இலரே share a common 'even if given' hyperbole, not a distinctive formula. Calling it a 'convention of comfort' from one friend's use, and citing line 104 of the idyll which the packet does not print, overclaims.

Natrinai 267's நொச்சி மா அரும்பு அன்ன கண்ண ... ஞெண்டு and Kar Narpathu 39's அலவன் கண் ஏய்ப்ப அரும்பு ஈன்று அவிழ்ந்த ... நொச்சி are one simile run in opposite directions. The observation that the crab is the shore poem's subject and the nochchi the mullai poem's is exact.
links.text_issue: Kar Narpathu 39 has a variant at line 2 (கருங்கதிர்) and a site difference at line 3.

links.reason: Spear that split the mountain and cock banner are shared (குன்றின் நெஞ்சுபக எறிந்த ... நெடுவேல் சேவலங் கொடியோன் / குலத்தைக் குத்திய வேலா ... கொடியோனே), the standard iconography of Murugan. The move from world to self reflects the difference between an anthology invocation and a petition song, not a change in the god's protection, so teaches generalises from genre.

Both put pallor in bed (பள்ளியுட் பாயும் பசப்பு / புல்லிக் கிடந்தேன் ... பசப்பு), a real but common link. Kar Narpathu 27 is about sulking at an absent man (ஊடி) and does not use the couplet's hyperbole of turning aside in an embrace, so the claim that it turns the Kural's figure into an argument is read in.
links.text_issue: Kar Narpathu 27 line 3 has a variant (பாராட்டில்).

links.reason: Ainkurunuru 360 makes the road easy (அரிய வாயினும் எளிய) by desire, and Akananuru 9 sends the heart ahead of the chariot (எம்மினும் விரைந்து வல்எய்தி). The contrast is accurate, but both are stock return poems and the 'two stages' framing adds little beyond the shared topic.

Natrinai 34 addresses the god (நின் அணங்கு அன்மை அறிந்தும் ... மடவை மன்ற வாழிய முருகே) and Natrinai 322 speaks for the hidden man to hear (அணங்கு என உணரக் கூறி வேலன் ... பலிக்கே), giving the cause as his chest not rightly had (உரிதினின் பெறாது). The same veri-refusal aimed at two audiences is specific.

An elephant with its mate in the heat is in both (பிடியோடு உறங்கும் / ஓய்பசிப் பிடியொடு ஒருதிறன் ஒடுங்க), a stock paalai image. In Akananuru 91 the comfort comes from பெரும்பேர் அன்பினர் and the refused Kudanadu, not from the elephants, so calling them the same iraicchi turned to comfort is unsupported.

The link depends on a tradition that neither text states, as the note admits; and Kalavazhi 39 says the Chola killed the Vanji king (வஞ்சிக்கோ அட்ட களத்து), which would sit ill with a captive king. A victory song and a captive's lament are not incompatible claims about one thing.

The sea crow with its காமர் பேடை / காமர் பெடை is a distinctive shared phrase in two neythal poems of neglect. In Natrinai 272 it feeds the pregnant hen (கடுஞ் சூல் ... அயிரை தேரிய), in Akananuru 170 it rests and dreams beside her at midnight, so the bird measures the man's failure in provision and in companionship.

Both have the rainbow (திருவில்) and the rains. In Ainkurunuru 428 they halt the chariots and end the king's task (வேந்துவிடு விழுத்தொழில் ஒழிய); in Akananuru 84 the king refuses tribute and moves on (அருந்திறை கொடுப்பவும் கொள்ளான்). The convention and its breaking are both in the Tamil.

Akananuru 44 sends the man home only after வந்துவினை முடித்தனன் வேந்தனும்; Patitruppattu 81 asks the king to yoke his chariot for one day (காணிய ஒருநாள் பூண்க) while the besieged keep their forts, so that துஞ்சா வேந்தரும் துஞ்சுக. The praise poem turning the mullai return into a call for a pause is accurate and specific.

The line (காலம்அறி யாதோன் கையுறல் பொய்) does make timing necessary. But Kural 484 joins time and place (காலம் கருதி இடத்தாற் செயின்), so it does not make timing alone 'enough'; the neat two halves of a condition rest on dropping the place.

Both have the kin clearing and ploughing (எறிந்தெமர் தாம்உழுத / எறிந்துழுது), and Thinaimalai 24 does turn it into a character (வெறும்புதல்போல் ... பிறர்நோய்க்கு நொந்தினைய வல்லளோ). The contrast is true but rests on a common kurinji phrase, so it is thin.

The Paripadal prayer (கிழவர் கிழவியர் என்னாது ஏழ்காறும் மழ ஈன்று மல்லற் கேள் மன்னுக) need not mean the same spouse across births: கேள் may be kin and ஏழ் generations. Teaches turns on one sense of those words and generalises one festival voice into a 'recognised petition of the Thai rite'.

Thinaimalai 56 only gives the shore lord the marks of the house (எம் முன்றில்), with the anril calling from the palmyras; it says nothing of nights apart. Teaches imports Natrinai 303's sleepless heroine (கேட்டொறும் துஞ்சாக் கண்ணள்) into a poem of kalavu, so the link rests on the shared stock bird.

Udhiyan is named in both, and Natrinai 113 uses the hushed field after his battle (உதியன் மண்டிய ஒலி தலை ஞாட்பின் இம்மென் பெருங் களத்து) for her sob, while Purananuru 2 praises his feeding (பெருஞ்சோற்று மிகுபதம் வரையாது கொடுத்தோய்). Teaches says what the akam poet does, but treats the two as one war, which neither poem says.

poems.note: A madal poem of open metaphors (காமக் கடல், காமன் படை); the only extended figure, the king restored to heaven, is joined by உறீஇயாங்கு.

iraicchi.act: having fed its fill on buds, sleeps at ease in the tangle of ripe pepper vine
iraicchi.sense: the man, having had his pleasure, rests unconcerned while the girl faces the mother's suspicion.

poems.note: The kumizh fruit feeding the deer sits inside the epithet of Ori's forest used for her hair's scent, so no sense for the lovers can be fixed.
The seizer of the drying fish is not named; the pairs are the theft for his taking and the fishermen's catch for her complexion she asks back.
The ambal feeding the bee in the cane bed points to another woman, but the poem states only the refusal of his embrace and the thurai is blank.

iraicchi.act: stays with longing heart searching for its doe and fawn that fled
iraicchi.sense: the man too, apart from his wife, longs to reach her, so the charioteer must hurry.

poems.note: The lizard's chirp is an omen of his return, a sign rather than an act of a person of the love.

iraicchi.act: feeds and frolics with its mate openly on the hilltop
iraicchi.sense: the friend hints that he should take the girl openly as the pair live, not by visits that set the street talking.

iraicchi.act: drives the hunters from the trough so its cow and calf may drink, then goes
iraicchi.sense: a man who sees such care for a mate on his road cannot forget his own wife and will return.

poems.note: சிறுபிடி துணையே is a direct address to the traveller, not a scene, so neither device applies.
பிற புலத் துணை hints at another woman, which the thurai (return from work) does not state; the absence, return and welcome pairs carry the tag.

iraicchi.act: drinks at the pool and frisks on the path together with its mate
iraicchi.sense: the man longs to be with her by evening, so the charioteer must drive fast.
